accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Dadabhai Naoroji:
1. He was one of the founding figures of the Indian National Congress.
2. He served as President of the Indian National Congress three times.
3. He was the first Indian elected to the British House of Commons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Dadabhai Naoroji helped found the INC, presided over it three times and became the first Indian elected to the British House of Commons.
accepted.tq: Verify each biographical statement separately before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Dadabhai Naoroji - role in founding, London activities, British Parliament  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Dadabhai Naoroji in chronological order:
A. Election to the British House of Commons
B. Establishment of the London Indian Society
C. Establishment of the East India Association
D. Service on the Welby Commission
accepted.x: The London Indian Society was established in 1865, the East India Association in 1866, his election took place in 1892 and he served on the Welby Commission in 1895.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then arrange the intermediate events.
accepted.sec: Dadabhai Naoroji - role in founding, London activities, British Parliament  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Dadabhai Naoroji delivered the first lecture of the East India Association on
accepted.x: The first lecture of the East India Association was delivered by Dadabhai Naoroji on 2 May 1867.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of the first lecture from the year of establishment of the organisation.
accepted.sec: Dadabhai Naoroji - role in founding, London activities, British Parliament  [APPSC]

accepted.x: In 1892, Dadabhai Naoroji was elected from Central Finsbury as a Liberal Party candidate.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding interpretations of the origin of the Indian National Congress:
1. R.P. Dutt described the safety-valve interpretation as a conspiracy to head off a popular uprising.
2. Bipan Chandra called the safety-valve theory a colonial myth.
3. Bipan Chandra used the expression 'lightning conductor' for Hume's role.
4. G.K. Gokhale also explained that an Indian could not have started the Congress because it would have faced official hostility.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. R.P. Dutt gave the conspiracy interpretation, while Bipan Chandra criticised the theory as a colonial myth and described Hume as a lightning conductor; Gokhale made the related point about official hostility.
accepted.tq: Separate the views of different historians and leaders before selecting the cumulative option.
accepted.sec: Safety-valve theory → proponents, critics and first user  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Lord Dufferin's role in the formation of the Indian National Congress is correct?
o: He probably suggested an annual meeting of educated Indians, but there is no proof that he proposed the INC.
He personally presided over the first session of the INC.
He formally founded the INC through an official proclamation in 1885.
He opposed every proposal for an annual forum of educated Indians.
accepted.x: Dufferin may have suggested an annual forum of educated Indians, but there is no proof that he proposed the establishment of the INC itself.
accepted.tq: Reject the stronger claim when the historical fact is limited to a probable suggestion.
accepted.sec: Safety-valve theory → proponents, critics and first user  [other exams]

accepted.s: The criticism that the safety-valve theory is a colonial myth is associated with
accepted.x: Bipan Chandra regarded the safety-valve theory as a colonial myth because Indians were already organising through bodies such as the Indian Association.
accepted.tq: Use the historian-interpretation association rather than the event narrative alone.
accepted.sec: Safety-valve theory → proponents, critics and first user  [other exams]

accepted.s: At the Madras session of the Indian National Congress in 1914, which of the following developments strengthened the demand for a separate Andhra Congress circle?
o: The adoption of a resolution creating a separate Andhra province
The participation of 256 Andhra delegates without any seat on the Working Committee
The election of an Andhra delegate as Congress President
The withdrawal of all Andhra delegates from the session
accepted.x: Although 256 Andhra delegates attended the Madras session in 1914, none obtained a Working Committee seat. This strengthened the demand for a separate Andhra Congress circle.
accepted.tq: Link the numerical detail with its political consequence in the same event.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about P. Anandacharlu is correct?
o: He was Secretary of the Indian Association in 1884 and became the first Bengali President of the INC.
He founded the East India Association in 1866 and became the first Telugu President of the INC.
He was Secretary of the Madras Mahajana Sabha in 1891 and became the first Tamil President of the INC.
He was Secretary of the Madras Mahajana Sabha in 1884 and became the first Telugu President of the INC.
accepted.x: P. Anandacharlu served as Secretary of the Madras Mahajana Sabha in 1884 and was the first Telugu President of the INC. He lived from 1843 to 1907.
accepted.tq: Combine the office, year and regional identity to distinguish a similar nationalist profile.

Consider the following statements about A.O. Hume:
1. He was a retired Indian Civil Service officer.
2. His relations with Lord Lytton were strained.
3. He was demoted in 1879 and retired in 1882.
4. He settled at Shimla after retirement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Hume was a retired ICS officer, had strained relations with Lytton, was demoted in 1879, retired in 1882 and then settled at Shimla.
accepted.tq: Check the complete biographical sequence rather than treating the statements as independent labels.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes A.O. Hume's political relationships and organisational role?
o: He avoided all regional political groups and served only as an adviser to the Viceroy.
He worked exclusively with the Madras leaders and became the first Treasurer of the INC.
He was closer to the Calcutta leaders than to the Bombay and Poona groups and became the first President of the INC.
He was closer to the Bombay and Poona groups than to the Calcutta leaders and became the first General Secretary of the INC.
accepted.x: Hume was closer to the Bombay and Poona groups than to the Calcutta leaders and served as the INC's first General Secretary.

Consider the following statements about Lord Dufferin's attitude towards the Indian National Congress:
1. He initially encouraged A.O. Hume's idea of an annual forum.
2. He later ridiculed the Congress as representing a 'microscopic minority'.
3. His criticism was expressed in 1888.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Dufferin initially encouraged the idea of an annual forum but later mocked the Congress as a microscopic minority in 1888.
accepted.tq: Track the change in attitude and attach the correct year to the later position.
accepted.sec: A.O. Hume - background, Viceroy Dufferin's attitude

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Lord Dufferin's attitude towards the Indian National Congress changed from initial encouragement to public ridicule.
Reason (R): He later described the Congress as representing a 'microscopic minority' in 1888.
Choose the correct answer.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, and Dufferin's later description of the Congress as a microscopic minority explains the change in his attitude.
accepted.tq: Check whether the reason directly accounts for the change stated in the assertion.
accepted.sec: A.O. Hume - background, Viceroy Dufferin's attitude

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Lord Ripon — Influence on Hume's interest in local self-government
A.O. Hume — Father of Indian Ornithology
A.O. Hume — First General Secretary of the INC
Lord Lytton — Initial encouragement of Hume's annual forum idea
accepted.x: Lord Dufferin, not Lord Lytton, initially encouraged Hume's idea of an annual forum. The other pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong authority by distinguishing the roles of neighbouring Viceroys.
accepted.sec: A.O. Hume - background, Viceroy Dufferin's attitude

accepted.s: Which of the following statements best reflects the distinction between the safety-valve and lightning-conductor interpretations?
o: The two views are identical and differ only in the date of the first Congress session.
The safety-valve view sees the Congress as an outlet for discontent, whereas the lightning-conductor view sees Hume as shielding the young organisation from official hostility.
The safety-valve view credits Indian leaders with shielding Hume, whereas the lightning-conductor view credits Dufferin with suppressing the Congress.
Both views hold that the Congress was created exclusively to obtain complete independence in 1885.
accepted.x: The safety-valve view presents the Congress as an outlet for discontent, while the lightning-conductor view presents Hume as a British intermediary who protected the infant organisation from official suppression.
accepted.tq: Contrast the central meaning of two easily confused historical interpretations.
